Read and write native n-dimensional measurement bundles

Source: R/nd-io.R
measure-nd-bundle.Rd

A native nD bundle is a directory containing a fixed manifest and three UTF-8 CSV or TSV tables. It preserves the ordered coordinates and values, dimension labels and units, list member order and labels, and the storage type of each numeric column. Sparse and repeated coordinate tuples are retained as observed.

Usage

write_measure_nd(x, path, delim = c(",", "\t"))

read_measure_nd(path, max_bytes = 100 * 1024^2)

Arguments

x

A structurally valid measure_nd_tbl or measure_nd_list using the standard core classes and supported attributes.

path

For writing, a new local directory path whose parent already exists. For reading, a directory containing a complete bundle.

delim

A comma or tab field delimiter used for all three payloads.

max_bytes

A positive whole-number limit for the actual cumulative bytes read from the manifest and the three selected payloads.

Value

write_measure_nd() returns the normalized destination path invisibly. read_measure_nd() returns a measure_nd_tbl or measure_nd_list matching the root kind stored in the bundle.

Details

The bundle format is a bounded numerical interchange profile. It does not store acquisition provenance, detector or sample identity, signal units, source row lineage, masks, or transformation history. The writer accepts only the standard core nD classes with attribute-free numeric and metadata vectors; unsupported attributes are rejected instead of being discarded. See the package's measure-nd-v1.md profile specification for the exact table and manifest schema.

The reader selects only the fixed payload names from the manifest. Other directory entries are ignored and are not protected by the manifest. Hashes detect payload changes but do not authenticate a bundle.

Bundle version 1

The fixed payloads are members.csv, axes.csv, and points.csv, or the corresponding .tsv files. The manifest has the exact fields Format, Version, Delimiter, Object-Type, Dimensions, List-Names, and -Rows, -Columns, and -SHA256 fields for each payload. The tables store member descriptors (including a list prototype at index 0), per-member axis metadata and storage types, and ordered numerical points. Member, axis, and point indices are explicit keys, so readers may restore order after table row reordering. Double tokens preserve NA, NaN, infinities and signed zero. The writer emits canonical finite decimal tokens; the reader also accepts equivalent finite spellings allowed by the scalar numeric parser.

Dimensions are limited to 2 through 1024. Existing objects with unsupported attributes, non-automatic row names, or attributed numeric or metadata vectors are outside this profile. The writer validates the full object before creating staging files, verifies its staged bundle with the strict reader, and never replaces an existing destination. A failed copy can leave an incomplete destination without a manifest; the reader rejects it.

Examples

measurement <- new_measure_nd_tbl(
  location_1 = c(1, 2, 2),
  location_2 = c(254L, 280L, 280L),
  value = c(0, -0, NA_real_),
  dim_names = c("time", "wavelength"),
  dim_units = c("min", "nm")
)
local({
  bundle <- tempfile("measure-nd-")
  on.exit(unlink(bundle, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  write_measure_nd(measurement, bundle)
  restored <- read_measure_nd(bundle)
  identical(measurement$location_2, restored$location_2)
})
#> [1] TRUE
